question: How do record and matched object references calibrate the preserved nested statistic under known independent, unique and literal-copy laws?
outcome: Three thousand observed populations and 396,000 references audited. At nominal 5%, independent records reject 5.0%, uniqueness-conditioned records 5.9%, and literal copies reject 5.4% with object references versus 15.9% with record references. Paired excess 10.5 points, 500-cluster interval 8.5–12.6.
challenge: Copied reference streams have 500 linked trial pairs; copying also changes the physical-block premise required for fitting support bounds.
remedy: Preserve actual seeds, audit all 928,424 proposals and p-values, replay 33 complete fits and resample linked clusters for the paired interval. Audit constructive component bounds separately.
retry_when: A new observation or selection law changes the conditional space; do not rerun the same frozen calibration merely to improve its rates.
